match.reason: No bank point lists the six landscape types in the brief (mountain, coastal, riverine, desert, karst and volcanic) with their typical landforms; the closest points define landscape versus landform or describe world landscape types without karst, volcanic or riverine, so a new point is needed.

draft.title: Types of landscapes
card: Landscapes are grouped into types by the main features that shape them. Each type has its own typical landforms.
high, steep land with peaks and ridges. Coastal landscapes sit where land meets the sea, with beaches, cliffs and headlands.
shaped by rivers, with channels, floodplains and billabongs. Desert landscapes are very dry, with features such as sand dunes and stony plains.
karst landscapes form in limestone, which water dissolves, leaving caves and sinkholes. Volcanic landscapes form from erupted lava and ash, with features such as volcanic cones and craters.
draft.remember: Each landscape type is known by its typical landforms, such as dunes in deserts and caves in karst.

a.q: A landscape is made mostly of limestone, with caves and sinkholes where water has dissolved the rock. Which type is it?
a.why: Karst landscapes form when water dissolves limestone, leaving caves and sinkholes. A volcanic landscape is the tempting choice for a landscape with holes, but its craters come from eruptions, not from dissolved rock.
a.clue: Think about which rock water can dissolve.

b.q: Sam visits a flat area with a wide floodplain and a billabong beside a winding river channel. Which type of landscape is Sam in?
b.why: Floodplains, billabongs and river channels are typical landforms of a riverine landscape, because they are shaped by a river. A coastal landscape is tempting because water is nearby, but it is found where land meets the sea, with beaches and cliffs.
b.clue: Which type is shaped mainly by a river?
